package com.hitorro.test.dms;

import com.hitorro.base.objects.Container;
import com.hitorro.base.objects.Document;
import com.hitorro.base.objects.VersionableObject;
import com.hitorro.basedms.session.DMSSessionFactory;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.EnhancedTestCase;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.HTTest;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.RunLevel;
import com.hitorro.util.typesystem.BaseSession;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Iterator;

/**
 * Copyright (c) 2003 - present HiTorro All rights reserved. User: chris Date: Oct 31, 2006 Time: 6:39:16 PM Tests related
 * to Containers of objects.
 */
@HTTest(runlevel = RunLevel.Smoke,
 email = "chris@hitorro.com",
 description = "Virtual container tests.")
public class ContainerTest extends EnhancedTestCase {
 /**
 * Basic container test, ensure that a sysobject can belong to more than one container and that we get all the right
 * objects back for a given container.
 */
 public void testBasicContainer() {
 BaseSession sess = DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().getCachedDMSSession();
 Container containerA = new Container(Document.class, "id");
 Container containerB = new Container(Document.class, "id");
 containerA.setDescription("Test Container A");
 sess.persist(containerA);
 containerB.setDescription("Test Container B");
 sess.persist(containerB);
 HashMap<String, String> mapA = new HashMap<String, String>();
 HashMap<String, String> mapB = new HashMap<String, String>();
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 // not sure whats going on here. hql shows the correct amount of results
 // dms.hql from ht.base.objects.Document s join s.containers c where c.id = 431
 Document both = createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, containerB);
 mapB.put(both.getGuid(), both.getGuid());
 DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().commitAndCloseSession(sess);
 // ensure that the container has both docs
 assertContainment(mapA, containerA);
 assertContainment(mapB, containerB);
 }

 private void assertContainment(HashMap<String, String> map, Container container) {
 BaseSession sessContainer = DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().getSession();
 container.setSession(sessContainer);
 Iterator<Object[]> soIter = container.getIterator();
 int i = 0;
		HashSet<String> found = new HashSet<String>();
 while (soIter.hasNext()) {
 Object a = soIter.next();
 VersionableObject so = (VersionableObject) a;
			found.add(so.getGuid());
 assertNotNull(map.get(so.getGuid()));
 i++;
 }
 assertEquals(map.size(), i);
 //DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().rollbackCloseSession(sessContainer);
 }

 private Document createDoc(BaseSession sess, HashMap<String, String> map, Container container, Container secondContainer) {
 Document d = new Document();
 d.setContent("ContentString");
 d.setNote("Document Note");
 d.setTitle("This is my document title");
 d.getContainers().add(container);
 if (secondContainer != null) {
 d.getContainers().add(secondContainer);
 }
 sess.persist(d);
 map.put(d.getGuid(), d.getGuid());
 return d;
 }
}

package com.hitorro.util.testframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.JUnitListener;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.core.ListUtil;

import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringListFromDelimitedKey;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.*;
import junit.framework.JUnit4TestAdapter;
import junit.framework.TestResult;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Test mechanism that deals with running a test or a suite of tests.
 */
public class TestUtil {
 public static StringProperty Level = new StringProperty("level", "unit test run-level", "smoke");
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Test = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("test", "specific unit test or tests that test a regexp string", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Tags = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("tags", "filter unit tests via string tags", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Packages = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("package", "listFiles of packages that are to be included", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Services = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("service", "listFiles of services that tests must be dependent on", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Modules = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("module", "listFiles of modules to be tested", ",", null);
 public static BooleanProperty IgnoreTestDependencies = new BooleanProperty("ignoretestdepends", "ignore the dependencies that a states it needs", false);

 public static BooleanProperty Shutdown = new BooleanProperty("shutdown", "shutdown after finished", false);

 public static BooleanProperty EnableService = new BooleanProperty("test.enableservice", "shutdown after finished", false);

 public static IntegerProperty WatchdogSeconds = new IntegerProperty("watchdogseconds", "How long the watchdog will wait", 5 * 60);

 public static TestWatchdogTimer timer = new TestWatchdogTimer();

 public static int runTest(final String test, final JsonNode map, final Response nestedResponse) throws TestException {
 //TestSuite suite = null;
 List<JUnit4TestAdapter> suites = new ArrayList();
 int exitCode = 0;
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(test)) {
 LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = getOperator(map);

 //suite = FilteredTestSuiteGenerator.getTestSuite(oper, null, IgnoreTestDependencies.apply(apply));
 suites = FilteredTestSuiteGenerator.getTestSuiteJ4(oper, null, IgnoreTestDependencies.apply(map));
 } else {
 TestCaseWrapper tcw = TestCaseWrapper.getWrapperIfAppropriate(test);
 if (tcw != null) {
 suites.add(new JUnit4TestAdapter(tcw.testClass));
 } else {
 throw new TestException(Fmt.S("Unable to find class %s or it not a subclass of %s",
 test, EnhancedTestCase.class.getCanonicalName()));
 }
 }
 JUnitListener l = new JUnitListener(nestedResponse, true);
 if (Shutdown.apply(map)) {
 // we have 5 minutes a test before we quit!
 timer.setTimeout(WatchdogSeconds.apply(map));
 timer.setResponse(nestedResponse, l);
 timer.start();
 }
 /* run test-suite */
 if (ListUtil.notNullAndContainsRows(suites)) {
 TestResult result = new TestResult();
 //suite.setName("Test Suite");

 result.addListener(l);
 for (JUnit4TestAdapter t : suites) {
 Log.test.info("Running testsuite %s", t);
 t.run(result);
 }

 nestedResponse.end();

 if (l.getErrorCount() > 0) {
 exitCode = 1;
 }
 }
 timer.stop();
 return exitCode;
 }

 public static LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> getOperator(final JsonNode map) {
 LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();

 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.RunLevelFilter(RunLevel.getFilterByName(Level.apply(map))));
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ServiceInitializedFilter());
 oper.addIfNotNull(getPackageConstraint(Packages.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getServiceConstraint(Services.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getModuleConstraint(Modules.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getTestConstraint(Test.apply(map)));
 // or listFiles of
 oper.addIfNotNull(getTagList(Tags.apply(map)));
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getPackageConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.PackagePrefixFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getServiceConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ServiceFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getModuleConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ModuleFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getTagList(List<String> tags) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(tags)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : tags) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.TagsFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getTestConstraint(List<String> tests) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(tests)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : tests) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.TestNameRegexpFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }
}

package com.hitorro.test.dms;

import com.hitorro.base.objects.Container;
import com.hitorro.base.objects.Document;
import com.hitorro.base.objects.VersionableObject;
import com.hitorro.basedms.session.DMSSessionFactory;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.EnhancedTestCase;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.HTTest;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.RunLevel;
import com.hitorro.util.typesystem.BaseSession;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Iterator;

/**
 * Copyright (c) 2003 - present HiTorro All rights reserved. User: chris Date: Oct 31, 2006 Time: 6:39:16 PM Tests related
 * to Containers of objects.
 */
@HTTest(runlevel = RunLevel.Smoke,
 email = "chris@hitorro.com",
 description = "Virtual container tests.")
public class ContainerTest extends EnhancedTestCase {
 /**
 * Basic container test, ensure that a sysobject can belong to more than one container and that we get all the right
 * objects back for a given container.
 */
 public void testBasicContainer() {
 BaseSession sess = DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().getCachedDMSSession();
 Container containerA = new Container(Document.class, "id");
 Container containerB = new Container(Document.class, "id");
 containerA.setDescription("Test Container A");
 sess.persist(containerA);
 containerB.setDescription("Test Container B");
 sess.persist(containerB);
 HashMap<String, String> mapA = new HashMap<String, String>();
 HashMap<String, String> mapB = new HashMap<String, String>();
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapB, containerB, null);
 createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, null);
 // not sure whats going on here. hql shows the correct amount of results
 // dms.hql from ht.base.objects.Document s join s.containers c where c.id = 431
 Document both = createDoc(sess, mapA, containerA, containerB);
 mapB.put(both.getGuid(), both.getGuid());
 DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().commitAndCloseSession(sess);
 // ensure that the container has both docs
 assertContainment(mapA, containerA);
 assertContainment(mapB, containerB);
 }

 private void assertContainment(HashMap<String, String> map, Container container) {
 BaseSession sessContainer = DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().getSession();
 container.setSession(sessContainer);
 Iterator<Object[]> soIter = container.getIterator();
 int i = 0;
		HashSet<String> found = new HashSet<String>();
 while (soIter.hasNext()) {
 Object a = soIter.next();
 VersionableObject so = (VersionableObject) a;
			found.add(so.getGuid());
 assertNotNull(map.get(so.getGuid()));
 i++;
 }
 assertEquals(map.size(), i);
 //DMSSessionFactory.getFactory().rollbackCloseSession(sessContainer);
 }

 private Document createDoc(BaseSession sess, HashMap<String, String> map, Container container, Container secondContainer) {
 Document d = new Document();
 d.setContent("ContentString");
 d.setNote("Document Note");
 d.setTitle("This is my document title");
 d.getContainers().add(container);
 if (secondContainer != null) {
 d.getContainers().add(secondContainer);
 }
 sess.persist(d);
 map.put(d.getGuid(), d.getGuid());
 return d;
 }
}

package com.hitorro.util.testframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.JUnitListener;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.core.ListUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.opers.HTPredicate;
import com.hitorro.util.core.opers.LogicalAndOperator;
import com.hitorro.util.core.opers.LogicalOrOperator;

import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.BooleanProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.IntegerProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringListFromDelimitedKey;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.*;
import junit.framework.JUnit4TestAdapter;
import junit.framework.TestResult;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Test mechanism that deals with running a test or a suite of tests.
 */
public class TestUtil {
 public static StringProperty Level = new StringProperty("level", "unit test run-level", "smoke");
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Test = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("test", "specific unit test or tests that test a regexp string", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Tags = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("tags", "filter unit tests via string tags", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Packages = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("package", "listFiles of packages that are to be included", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Services = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("service", "listFiles of services that tests must be dependent on", ",", null);
 public static StringListFromDelimitedKey Modules = new StringListFromDelimitedKey("module", "listFiles of modules to be tested", ",", null);
 public static BooleanProperty IgnoreTestDependencies = new BooleanProperty("ignoretestdepends", "ignore the dependencies that a states it needs", false);

 public static BooleanProperty Shutdown = new BooleanProperty("shutdown", "shutdown after finished", false);

 public static BooleanProperty EnableService = new BooleanProperty("test.enableservice", "shutdown after finished", false);

 public static IntegerProperty WatchdogSeconds = new IntegerProperty("watchdogseconds", "How long the watchdog will wait", 5 * 60);

 public static TestWatchdogTimer timer = new TestWatchdogTimer();

 public static int runTest(final String test, final JsonNode map, final Response nestedResponse) throws TestException {
 //TestSuite suite = null;
 List<JUnit4TestAdapter> suites = new ArrayList();
 int exitCode = 0;
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(test)) {
 LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = getOperator(map);

 //suite = FilteredTestSuiteGenerator.getTestSuite(oper, null, IgnoreTestDependencies.apply(apply));
 suites = FilteredTestSuiteGenerator.getTestSuiteJ4(oper, null, IgnoreTestDependencies.apply(map));
 } else {
 TestCaseWrapper tcw = TestCaseWrapper.getWrapperIfAppropriate(test);
 if (tcw != null) {
 suites.add(new JUnit4TestAdapter(tcw.testClass));
 } else {
 throw new TestException(Fmt.S("Unable to find class %s or it not a subclass of %s",
 test, EnhancedTestCase.class.getCanonicalName()));
 }
 }
 JUnitListener l = new JUnitListener(nestedResponse, true);
 if (Shutdown.apply(map)) {
 // we have 5 minutes a test before we quit!
 timer.setTimeout(WatchdogSeconds.apply(map));
 timer.setResponse(nestedResponse, l);
 timer.start();
 }
 /* run test-suite */
 if (ListUtil.notNullAndContainsRows(suites)) {
 TestResult result = new TestResult();
 //suite.setName("Test Suite");

 result.addListener(l);
 for (JUnit4TestAdapter t : suites) {
 Log.test.info("Running testsuite %s", t);
 t.run(result);
 }

 nestedResponse.end();

 if (l.getErrorCount() > 0) {
 exitCode = 1;
 }
 }
 timer.stop();
 return exitCode;
 }

 public static LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> getOperator(final JsonNode map) {
 LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalAndOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();

 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.RunLevelFilter(RunLevel.getFilterByName(Level.apply(map))));
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ServiceInitializedFilter());
 oper.addIfNotNull(getPackageConstraint(Packages.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getServiceConstraint(Services.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getModuleConstraint(Modules.apply(map)));
 oper.addIfNotNull(getTestConstraint(Test.apply(map)));
 // or listFiles of
 oper.addIfNotNull(getTagList(Tags.apply(map)));
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getPackageConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.PackagePrefixFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getServiceConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ServiceFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getModuleConstraint(List<String> pack) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(pack)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : pack) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.ModuleFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;

 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getTagList(List<String> tags) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(tags)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : tags) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.TagsFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }

 public static final HTPredicate<TestCaseWrapper> getTestConstraint(List<String> tests) {
 if (ListUtil.nullOrEmpty(tests)) {
 return null;
 }
 LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper> oper = new LogicalOrOperator<TestCaseWrapper>();
 for (String p : tests) {
 oper.add(new com.hitorro.util.testframework.filters.TestNameRegexpFilter(p));
 }
 oper.finalizeFilter();
 return oper;
 }
}

package com.hitorro.util.startupframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.propreaders.JVSProperties;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.Fmt;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.StringUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.propaccess.PropaccessError;
import com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDefinition;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@ServiceDefinition(dependentService = {},
 shortName = "server",
 description = "Service startup service",
 debugCommands = {},
 generatedServices = true
)
public class HTServer extends RunnableService {
 public static final StringProperty NodeId = new StringProperty("node", "id of node if server is a multinodel server", null);
 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceProperty
 public final StringProperty ServerType = new StringProperty("servertype", "type of server to start", null);
 private String serverType;
 private JsonNode serverProps = null;

 public List<Class> getDependentService() {
 serverType = ServerType.apply();
 JVS jvs = JVSProperties.getProperties();
 String server = Fmt.S("services.%s", serverType);
 try {
 serverProps = jvs.get(server);
 } catch (PropaccessError propaccessError) {
 return null;
 }
 if (serverProps != null) {
 List<Class> dependencies = new ArrayList<Class>();
 for (JsonNode e : serverProps) {
 String s = e.textValue();
 Class clazz = ClassUtil.getClassForName(s, null);
 if (clazz != null) {
 dependencies.add(clazz);
 } else {
 Log.servicecontext.fatal("Dependent service %s does not have a corresponding class to initialize", s);
 }
 }
 return dependencies;
 }
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceInit
 public String init(boolean dbInit, final boolean upgrading, final long currentVersion, final long targetVersion) {
 if (serverProps == null || serverProps.size() == 0) {
 return Fmt.S("Unable to initialize HTServer, service %s is not defined in the services file.", serverType);
 }
 return null;
 }

 public String run() {
 ServiceContext.waitForDeInit();
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDeInit
 public String deInit() {
 return null;
 }

 public String getShortName() {
 String nodeId = NodeId.apply();
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(nodeId)) {
 return Fmt.S("Server-%s", ServerType.apply());
 }

 return Fmt.S("%s-%s", ServerType.apply(), nodeId);
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceStart
 public String start(boolean dbInit) {
 return null;
 }

}

 public static EnumContext<RedirectEnum> redirectContext;

 RedirectEnum(String shortName, String description, String arg, String noArg) {

 this.arg = arg;

 setMapEntry(this, shortName);

 public static final File determineBINFromClasspath() {
 URL u = ClassLoader.getSystemResource("config.txt");
 if (u == null) {
 return null;
 }
 String propsDirFile = u.toExternalForm();
 File f = null;
 try {
 URL url = new URL(propsDirFile);
 f = new File(url.getFile());
 } catch (MalformedURLException e) {
 return null;
 }
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyString(propsDirFile)) {
 return null;
 }
 if (f == null) {
 return null;
 }
 f = f.getParentFile().getParentFile();
 return f;

 }

 /**
 * This function doesnt seem to work very well for the purpose of getting a blind IP address there can be ipv6 and
 * docker ip addresses when one just onces a meaningfull ipv4 adderss to ping this host.
 *
 * @return
 */
 public static final String getHostIPFromNetworkInterfaces() {
 try {
 Enumeration e = NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces();
 List<String> hosts = new ArrayList();
 while (e.hasMoreElements()) {
 NetworkInterface n = (NetworkInterface) e.nextElement();
 Enumeration ee = n.getInetAddresses();
 while (ee.hasMoreElements()) {
 InetAddress i = (InetAddress) ee.nextElement();
 hosts.add(i.getHostAddress());
 }
 }
 if (hosts.size() > 1) {
 return hosts.get(1);
 }
 return hosts.get(0);
 } catch (SocketException e) {
 Log.util.error("Unable to get hostIP %s %e", e, e);
 return null;
 }
 }

 /**

 public static final String getPrettyPrintedProperties(Map props) {
 StringBuilder buff = new StringBuilder();
 Iterator iter = MapUtil.keyIterator(props);
 buff.append("Process java properties: \n");
 while (iter.hasNext()) {
 String key = (String) iter.next();
 buff.append(key);
 buff.append(" = ");
 buff.append(props.get(key));
 buff.append(Constants.NewLineChar);
 }
 return buff.toString();
 }

 /**

 *
 * @param seconds
 * @return true if waited, false if interrupted.
 */
 public static final boolean sleepNSeconds(int seconds) {
 try {
 Thread.sleep(seconds * Constants.MillisInSecond);
 return true;
 } catch (InterruptedException e) {
 return false;
 }
 }

 /**
 * Wait on an object getting notified, or a timeout occuring.
 *
 * @param seconds
 * @param lock
 * @return
 */
 public static final boolean sleepNSeconds(int seconds, Object lock) {
 synchronized (lock) {
 try {
 lock.wait(seconds * Constants.MillisInSecond);
 return true;
 } catch (InterruptedException e) {
 return false;
 }
 }
 }

 /**
 * Make the thread wait n seconds.
 *
 * @param millis
 * @return true if waited, false if interrupted.
 */
 public static final boolean sleepMillis(long millis) {
 try {
 Thread.sleep(millis);
 return true;
 } catch (InterruptedException e) {
 return false;
 }
 }

 /**
 * Get the stack trace of the caller and return it as a String
 *
 * @return
 */
 public static final String getCurrentStackTrace() {
 try {
 throw new Exception("ExceptionUsedForStackTraceOnly");
 } catch (Exception ex) {
 StackTraceElement[] stacks = ex.getStackTrace();
 StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder();
 // ignore top frame - that's us
 for (int i = 1; i < stacks.length; i++) {
 buf.append(stacks[i].toString()).append("\n");
 }
 return buf.toString();
 }
 }

 public static void getHeapMemoryInfo(Map<String, Object> map) {
 MemoryMXBean bean = ManagementFactory.getMemoryMXBean();
 int count = bean.getObjectPendingFinalizationCount();

 MemoryUsage mu = bean.getHeapMemoryUsage();
 addRow(map, "HeapMemoryUsage.ObjectsPendingFinalization", Long.toString(count));
 addRow(map, "HeapMemoryUsage.Commited", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(mu.getCommitted()));

 addRow(map, "HeapMemoryUsage.Init", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(mu.getInit()));
 addRow(map, "HeapMemoryUsage.Max", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(mu.getMax()));
 addRow(map, "HeapMemoryUsage.Used", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(mu.getUsed()));
 MemoryUsage nonHeap = bean.getNonHeapMemoryUsage();
 addRow(map, "NonHeapMemoryUsage.Commited", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(nonHeap.getCommitted()));

 addRow(map, "NonHeapMemoryUsage.Init", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(nonHeap.getInit()));
 addRow(map, "NonHeapMemoryUsage.Max", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(nonHeap.getMax()));
 addRow(map, "NonHeapMemoryUsage.Used", StringUtil.getBytesNeatForm(nonHeap.getUsed()));
 }

 public static void getOSInfo(Map<String, Object> map) {
 OperatingSystemMXBean osBean = ManagementFactory.getOperatingSystemMXBean();
 if (osBean instanceof UnixOperatingSystemMXBean) {
 UnixOperatingSystemMXBean uosBean = (UnixOperatingSystemMXBean) osBean;
 addRow(map, "build.openfiledescriptors", uosBean.getOpenFileDescriptorCount());
 addRow(map, "build.maxfiledescriptors", uosBean.getMaxFileDescriptorCount());
 addRow(map, "build.totalswap", uosBean.getTotalSwapSpaceSize());
 addRow(map, "build.processscputime", uosBean.getProcessCpuTime());


 addRow(map, "build.commitedvirtual", uosBean.getCommittedVirtualMemorySize());
 addRow(map, "build.freephysicalmemory", uosBean.getFreePhysicalMemorySize());
 addRow(map, "build.freeswapspace", uosBean.getFreeSwapSpaceSize());
 addRow(map, "build.availProcessors", uosBean.getAvailableProcessors());

 if (Platform.getPlatform().isUnixVariant()) {
 // HACK because java 1.5 on a mac does not have this method.
 Class c = uosBean.getClass();

 try {
 Method m = c.getMethod("getSystemLoadAverage");
 Object arguments[] = {};
 Object o = m.invoke(uosBean, arguments);
 addRow(map, "os.loadAverage", o);

 } catch (NoSuchMethodException e) {

 } catch (InvocationTargetException e) {

 } catch (IllegalAccessException e) {

 }
 }
 }
 addRow(map, "os.Architecture", osBean.getArch());
 addRow(map, "os.name", osBean.getName());
 addRow(map, "os.version", osBean.getVersion());
 }

 public static void getGCInfo(Map<String, Object> map) {
 List<GarbageCollectorMXBean> gcMXBeans = ManagementFactory.getGarbageCollectorMXBeans();
 if (gcMXBeans != null && gcMXBeans.size() > 0) {

 for (GarbageCollectorMXBean gcMXBean : gcMXBeans) {
 if (gcMXBean.getCollectionCount() > 0) {
 addRow(map, "gc.mode", gcMXBean.getName());
 addRow(map, "g.ccollections", Long.toString(gcMXBean.getCollectionCount()));
 addRow(map, "gc.approximatTimeSeconds", Long.toString(gcMXBean.getCollectionTime() / 1000));
 }
 }
 }

 }

 @CommandDef(command = "r", description = "redirect")
 public static RedirectHttp redirect(@DebugArgAno(keyName = "",
 description = "",
 defaultValue = "",
 argType = ArgType.Raw) String raw,
 @DebugArgAno(keyName = "",
 description = "",
 defaultValue = "",
 argType = ArgType.Args) JVS args,
 @DebugArgAno(keyName = "",
 description = "",
 defaultValue = "",
 argType = ArgType.Uri) String uri,
 @DebugArgAno(keyName = "",
 description = "",
 defaultValue = "",
 argType = ArgType.Request) HttpServletRequest req
 ) {
 RedirectHttp http = new RedirectHttp();
 String lineRaw = null;
 try {
 lineRaw = args.getString("q");
 } catch (PropaccessError propaccessError) {
 return null;
 }
 String parts[] = StringUtil.splitByToken(lineRaw, ' ');
 if (parts.length >= 1) {
 RedirectEnum r = RedirectEnum.redirectContext.getByShortName(parts[0]);
 if (r == null) {
 r = RedirectEnum.g;
 }
 if (parts.length == 1) {
 http.setPath(r.getWithoutArg());
 } else {
 http.setPath(r.getWithArg(parts[1]));
 }
 }
 return http;
 }

Now let me create a simple README to document the usage:"}],"tool_calls":[{"id":"toolu_01A8E5R4uw9GPQTDfgKijJQ9","type":"function","function":{"name":"write","arguments":"{"file_path": "/Users/chris/hitorro/hitorro-util/CPU_INFO_README.md", "content": "# CPU Information Utilities\n\n## Overview\n\nThe `CPUInfo` class provides cross-platform utility functions to retrieve CPU information, specifically CPU clock speed, on Linux and Mac OS X systems.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Cross-platform support**: Works on Linux and Mac OS X\n- **Multiple detection methods**: Uses platform-specific approaches for accurate results\n- **Convenient return formats**: Get speed in MHz, GHz, or as a formatted string\n- **Apple Silicon support**: Gracefully handles Apple Silicon Macs where fixed clock speeds are not available\n\n## Usage\n\n### Get CPU Clock Speed (Full Information)\n\n```java\nimport com.hitorro.util.core.CPUInfo;\nimport com.hitorro.util.core.CPUInfo.ClockSpeed;\n\nClockSpeed speed = CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeed();\nif (speed != null) {\n System.out.println(\"CPU Speed: \" + speed);\n System.out.println(\"MHz: \" + speed.getSpeedMHz());\n System.out.println(\"GHz: \" + speed.getSpeedGHz());\n System.out.println(\"Source: \" + speed.getSource());\n} else {\n System.out.println(\"Unable to determine CPU clock speed\");\n}\n```\n\n### Get CPU Clock Speed in MHz\n\n```java\ndouble mhz = CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeedMHz();\nif (mhz > 0) {\n System.out.println(\"CPU Speed: \" + mhz + \" MHz\");\n}\n```\n\n### Get CPU Clock Speed in GHz\n\n```java\ndouble ghz = CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeedGHz();\nif (ghz > 0) {\n System.out.println(\"CPU Speed: \" + ghz + \" GHz\");\n}\n```\n\n### Get Formatted String\n\n```java\nString formatted = CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeedFormatted();\nSystem.out.println(\"CPU Speed: \" + formatted);\n```\n\n## Platform-Specific Behavior\n\n### Linux\n\nOn Linux systems, the utility reads from `/proc/cpuinfo` and parses the \"cpu MHz\" field. If multiple cores report different speeds (e.g., due to dynamic frequency scaling), the average speed across all cores is returned.\n\nExample `/proc/cpuinfo` entry:\n```\ncpu MHz : 2600.000\n```\n\n### Mac OS X (Intel)\n\nOn Intel-based Macs, the utility uses `sysctl` to query hardware information:\n1. First tries `hw.cpufrequency` (returns Hz)\n2. Falls back to `hw.cpufrequency_max`\n3. Falls back to parsing `machdep.cpu.brand_string` (e.g., \"Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz\")\n\n### Mac OS X (Apple Silicon)\n\nOn Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4, etc.), fixed CPU clock speeds are not exposed through traditional sysctl interfaces because these chips use advanced dynamic frequency scaling with performance and efficiency cores running at different speeds.\n\nThe utility will:\n- Attempt all detection methods\n- Log the chip information (e.g., \"Apple M4 Max\")\n- Return `null` as there is no single fixed clock speed\n\nThis is expected behavior and not an error - Apple Silicon CPUs dynamically adjust their frequency based on workload.\n\n## Command Definitions\n\nThe following commands are available for command-line or RPC invocation:\n\n- `cpu.clockspeed` - Get full ClockSpeed object\n- `cpu.clockspeed.mhz` - Get speed in MHz as double\n- `cpu.clockspeed.ghz` - Get speed in GHz as double\n- `cpu.clockspeed.formatted` - Get formatted string representation\n\n## Return Values\n\n### ClockSpeed Object\n\nThe `ClockSpeed` class contains:\n- `speedMHz` (double) - Clock speed in megahertz\n- `speedGHz` (double) - Clock speed in gigahertz (speedMHz / 1000)\n- `source` (String) - The method/source used to determine the speed\n\n### Null Returns\n\nMethods return `null` or `-1.0` (for numeric methods) when:\n- The platform is not supported (not Linux or Mac)\n- The detection method fails\n- The information is not available (e.g., Apple Silicon Macs)\n\n## Error Handling\n\nThe utility handles errors gracefully:\n- Logs warnings for unsupported platforms\n- Logs errors for I/O failures or parsing issues\n- Returns `null` or `-1.0` instead of throwing exceptions\n\n## Example Output\n\n### Intel Mac\n```\n2.60 GHz (2600 MHz) [sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string]\n```\n\n### Linux System\n```\n3.40 GHz (3400 MHz) [/proc/cpuinfo]\n```\n\n### Apple Silicon Mac\n```\nUnknown\n```\n(With log message: \"Apple Silicon detected: Apple M4 Max (dynamic frequency scaling -  51|		
 52|		public ClockSpeed(double speedMHz, String source) {
 53|			this.speedMHz = speedMHz;
 54|			this.speedGHz = speedMHz / 1000.0;
 55|			this.source = source;
 56|		}

 58|		public double getSpeedMHz() {
 59|			return speedMHz;

 76|	/**
 77|	 * Get the CPU clock speed in MHz.
 78|	 * This method works on both Linux and Mac OS X.
 79|	 *
 80|	 * @return ClockSpeed object containing speed information, or null if unable to determine
 81|	 */
 82|	@CommandDef(command = "cpu.clockspeed", description = "Get CPU clock speed")
 83|	public static ClockSpeed getCPUClockSpeed() {
 84|		Platform platform = Platform.getPlatform();
 85|		
 86|		if (platform == Platform.Linux) {
 87|			return getLinuxCPUClockSpeed();
 88|		} else if (platform == Platform.MacOSX) {
 89|			return getMacCPUClockSpeed();
 90|		}

 92|		Log.util.warn("CPU clock speed detection not supported for platform: %s", platform.getShortName());
 93|		return null;
 94|	}

 96|	/**
 97|	 * Get CPU clock speed on Linux systems.
 98|	 * Reads from /proc/cpuinfo and parses the "cpu MHz" field.
 99|	 *
100|	 * @return ClockSpeed object or null if unable to determine
101|	 */
102|	private static ClockSpeed getLinuxCPUClockSpeed() {
103|		File cpuInfo = new File("/proc/cpuinfo");
104|		if (!cpuInfo.exists()) {
105|			Log.util.warn("Cannot read /proc/cpuinfo");
106|			return null;
107|		}
108|		
109|		try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(cpuInfo))) {
110|			Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile("cpu\\s+MHz\\s*:\\s*([0-9.]+)");
111|			String line;
112|			List<Double> speeds = new ArrayList<>();
113|			
114|			while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
115|				Matcher matcher = pattern.matcher(line);
116|				if (matcher.find()) {
117|					double mhz = Double.parseDouble(matcher.group(1));
118|					speeds.add(mhz);
119|				}
120|			}
121|			
122|			if (!speeds.isEmpty()) {
123|				// Return average speed across all cores
124|				double avgSpeed = speeds.stream().mapToDouble(Double::doubleValue).average().orElse(0.0);
125|				return new ClockSpeed(avgSpeed, "/proc/cpuinfo");
126|			}
127|		} catch (Exception e) {
128|			Log.util.error("Error reading CPU clock speed from /proc/cpuinfo: %s %e", e, e);
129|		}
130|		
131|		return null;
132|	}

package com.hitorro.util.startupframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.propreaders.JVSProperties;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;

import com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDefinition;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@ServiceDefinition(dependentService = {},
 shortName = "server",
 description = "Service startup service",
 debugCommands = {},
 generatedServices = true
)
public class HTServer extends RunnableService {
 public static final StringProperty NodeId = new StringProperty("node", "id of node if server is a multinodel server", null);
 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceProperty
 public final StringProperty ServerType = new StringProperty("servertype", "type of server to start", null);
 private String serverType;
 private JsonNode serverProps = null;

 public List<Class> getDependentService() {
 serverType = ServerType.apply();
 JVS jvs = JVSProperties.getProperties();
 String server = Fmt.S("services.%s", serverType);
 try {
 serverProps = jvs.get(server);
 } catch (PropaccessError propaccessError) {
 return null;
 }
 if (serverProps != null) {
 List<Class> dependencies = new ArrayList<Class>();
 for (JsonNode e : serverProps) {
 String s = e.textValue();
 Class clazz = ClassUtil.getClassForName(s, null);
 if (clazz != null) {
 dependencies.add(clazz);
 } else {
 Log.servicecontext.fatal("Dependent service %s does not have a corresponding class to initialize", s);
 }
 }
 return dependencies;
 }
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceInit
 public String init(boolean dbInit, final boolean upgrading, final long currentVersion, final long targetVersion) {
 if (serverProps == null || serverProps.size() == 0) {
 return Fmt.S("Unable to initialize HTServer, service %s is not defined in the services file.", serverType);
 }
 return null;
 }

 public String run() {
 ServiceContext.waitForDeInit();
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDeInit
 public String deInit() {
 return null;
 }

 public String getShortName() {
 String nodeId = NodeId.apply();
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(nodeId)) {
 return Fmt.S("Server-%s", ServerType.apply());
 }

 return Fmt.S("%s-%s", ServerType.apply(), nodeId);
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceStart
 public String start(boolean dbInit) {
 return null;
 }

}

import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.InfoLevel;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.Fmt;

/**
 * .
 */
public class UnitTimeResult {
 public double milliSecondsPerUnit;
	public double nsPerUnit;
 public double units;
 public String category;
 public String subCategory;
 public String description;
 public Class unitClass;

 public Exception error;


 public String toString() {
 return Fmt.S("millispu: %s, nspu: %s, units: %s, cat: %s, subcat: %s, uclass:%s",
 milliSecondsPerUnit, nsPerUnit, units, category, subCategory, ClassUtil.getBareName(unitClass));
 }

 public void addToRow(Response row) {
 if (error != null) {
 row.addInfo(InfoLevel.Error, Fmt.S("Unhandled exception in %s %s %e", description, error, error));
 } else {
 row.addRow(Double.toString(milliSecondsPerUnit),
					Double.toString(nsPerUnit),
 Double.toString(units),
 category,
 subCategory,
 description,
 ClassUtil.getBareName(unitClass));
 }
 }
}

 15|/**
 16| * Copyright (c) 2003 - present HiTorro All rights reserved. User: chris Date: Nov 22, 2006 Time: 11:50:32 PM
 17| * <p/>
 18| * Find all timer tests that meet a criteria and then measure the amount of time taken to execute.
 19| * <p/>
 20| * We compute a number of things: 1) resolution of system clock. 2) cost of making a method call 3) cost of doing a
 21| * simple piece of work such as assignment that is assumed to be about 1 instruction
 22| * <p/>
 23| * From this we can compute what other things cost in both ms and machine instructions.
 24| */
 25|
 26|public class UnitTimeContext {
 27| /* The precision, in milliseconds, of System.currentTimeMillis (). */
 28| public static double m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs = 0.0;
 29|
 30| /* The requested maximum relative error. */
 31| public static double error = 0.01;
 32|
 33| /* The minimum duration of tests needed to achieve the maximum
 34| relative "error". */
 35| public static double minExecutionTimeMsecs = 0.0;
 36|
 37| /* The overhead of doing one iteration of a test. */
 38| public static double m_invokationOverheadMSecs = 0.0;
 39|
 40| /* The cost of doing a local assignment, used as the machine-independent
 41| "unit". */
 42| public static double m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs = 0.0;
 43| private static UnitTimeContext utc = new UnitTimeContext();
 44| private boolean isInitialized = false;
 45|
 46| public static UnitTimeContext getUnitTimeContext() {
 47| return utc;
 48| }
 49|
 50| /**
 51| * During initialization we need to compute a few things:
 52| * <p/>
 53| * 1) Resolution of the system clock, this determines how much error there is in measuring runtime of a test. 2)
 54| * Baseline cost of making a call to a test function (so it can be subtracted out of tests). 3) Baseline unit cost.
 55| * Take an instruction that we know to be 1 cycle typically on a processor and use that as our "Unit". All other

194| public final UnitTimeResult executeTest(UnitTimer unit) {
195| if (isInitialized == false) {
196| init(null, 0.005);
197| }
198| // attempt to jit.
199| UnitTimeResult result = new UnitTimeResult();
200|
201| try {
202| unit.init();
203|
204| unit.preTest();
205| try {
206| unit.test();
207| } finally {
208| unit.postTest();
209| }
210|
211| long n = 1;
212| double runTimeInMillis = 0;
213| double startTimeInMillis = 0;
214| double requiredExecTimeInMSecs = minExecutionTimeMsecs;
215|
216|
217| if (unit.getTotalMsecs() > 0) {
218| requiredExecTimeInMSecs = unit.getTotalMsecs();
219| }
220|
221| try {
222| unit.preTest();
223| while (true) {
224| System.gc();
225|
226| startTimeInMillis = System.currentTimeMillis();
227| for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
228| unit.test();
229| }
230| runTimeInMillis = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTimeInMillis;
231|
232|
233| if (runTimeInMillis >= requiredExecTimeInMSecs) {
234| // we have hit our target time
235| break;
236| } else {
237| if (runTimeInMillis < 10 * m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs) {
238| n = 2 * n;
239| } else {
240| n = (long) Math.max(1.1 * n,
241| requiredExecTimeInMSecs / (runTimeInMillis - m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs) * n);
242| }
243| if (n < 0) {
244|
245| Log.util.error("Unit test loop overflow");
246| break;
247| }
248| }
249| }
250| } finally {
251| unit.postTest();
252| }
253| // what does it cost to make 1 call
254| double individualCallTime = (runTimeInMillis / n) - m_invokationOverheadMSecs;
255| if (individualCallTime < 0) {
256| // we are not that precise. This call looks like it runs approx same as a invokation call
257| // jit could of defeated us. I dont like negative values so lets make it a baseline unit cost
258| // we should perhaps consider running the tests again
259| Log.util.error("Reseting call time to baseline since it is negative (could be defeated by jit)");
260| individualCallTime = m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs;
261| }
262| // take account that 1 call my run whatever we are testing n times, then take account of the call cost
263| double milliSecondsPerUnit = (individualCallTime / unit.getIterations()) - unit.getBaseMsecsPerTest();
264|
265| // we have an approx baseline for what a unit costs to execute (proxy for instruction cycle)
266| double units = milliSecondsPerUnit / m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs;
267|
268| result.milliSecondsPerUnit = milliSecondsPerUnit;
269|			result.nsPerUnit = milliSecondsPerUnit * 1000000;
270| result.units = units;
271| result.category = unit.getCategory();
272| result.subCategory = unit.getSubCategory();
273| result.description = unit.getDescription();
274| result.unitClass = unit.getClass();
275|
276| Log.unitTime.debug("%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s",
277| Double.toString(milliSecondsPerUnit),
278|					Double.toString(result.nsPerUnit),
279| Double.toString(units),
280| unit.getCategory(),
281| unit.getSubCategory(),
282| unit.getDescription(),
283| ClassUtil.getBareName(unit.getClass()));
284| if (units < 0) {
285| Log.unitTime.info("Units < 0 %s, n=%s, m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs=%s", Double.toString(units), n, m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs);
286| }
287|
288|
289| } catch (Exception e) {
290| result.error = e;
291| result.milliSecondsPerUnit = 0.0;
292| }
293| return result;
294| }

This provides insight into approximately how many CPU clock cycles each Java operation requires.\n\n## Changes Made\n\n### 1. UnitTimeCommand.java\n- **CPU Detection**: Added automatic CPU clock speed detection using `CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeed()`\n- **Default Fallback**: Falls back to 4.0 GHz if detection fails\n- **New Column**: Added `instruction_cycles` column to response definition\n- **Logging**: Logs detected or default CPU speed for transparency\n\n### 2. UnitTimeResult.java\n- **New Field**: Added `public double instructionCycles` field\n- **Updated Methods**: Modified `toString()` and `addToRow()` to include instruction cycles\n\n### 3. UnitTimeContext.java\n- **CPU GHz Storage**: Added `cpuGigahertz` field to store CPU clock speed\n- **Updated Signature**: `runTests()` now accepts `cpuGigahertz` parameter\n- **Cycle Calculation**: Added instruction cycle computation in `executeTest()` method\n\n## Instruction Cycle Calculation Formula\n\nThe calculation is based on the fundamental relationship between time and CPU clock speed:\n\n```\nInstruction Cycles = Nanoseconds × CPU Frequency (GHz)\n```\n\n### Mathematical Explanation\n\n1. **CPU Frequency in GHz** means billions of cycles per second\n - Example: 3.0 GHz = 3,000,000,000 cycles/second\n\n2. **One nanosecond** is one-billionth of a second\n - 1 ns = 1 / 1,000,000,000 seconds\n\n3. **Cycles per nanosecond** = GHz value\n - At 3.0 GHz: 3 cycles per nanosecond\n - At 4.0 GHz: 4 cycles per nanosecond\n\n4. **Total cycles** = nanoseconds × cycles per nanosecond\n - If operation takes 10 ns at 3.0 GHz: 10 × 3 = 30 cycles\n - If operation takes 10 ns at 4.0 GHz: 10 × 4 = 40 cycles\n\n### Implementation\n\n```java\n// nsPerUnit is already computed (milliseconds * 1,000,000)\n// cpuGigahertz is detected or defaulted to 4.0\nif (cpuGigahertz > 0) {\n result.instructionCycles = result.nsPerUnit * cpuGigahertz;\n}\n```\n\n## Example Results\n\n### Intel CPU @ 2.6 GHz\n\n| Operation | ns/unit | Instruction Cycles |\n|-----------|---------|-------------------|\n| Local Assignment | 0.5 ns | 1.3 cycles |\n| Integer Addition | 1.0 ns | 2.6 cycles |\n| Float Multiplication | 2.0 ns | 5.2 cycles |\n| Array Access | 3.5 ns | 9.1 cycles |\n\n### Apple M4 Max (Detection Not Available)\n\nOn Apple Silicon, CPU frequency detection returns `null` because these chips use dynamic frequency scaling with performance and efficiency cores. The system will:\n- Use the default 4.0 GHz value\n- Log a warning message\n- Still provide meaningful relative cycle estimates\n\n| Operation | ns/unit | Instruction Cycles (est.) |\n|-----------|---------|--------------------------|\n| Local Assignment | 0.5 ns | 2.0 cycles (estimated) |\n| Integer Addition | 1.0 ns | 4.0 cycles (estimated) |\n\n## Assumptions and Limitations\n\n### Key Assumption\n**One instruction per cycle**: The calculation assumes a theoretical CPU where each clock cycle can execute one instruction. This is a simplification.\n\n### Real-World Considerations\n\n1. **Superscalar CPUs**: Modern CPUs can execute multiple instructions per cycle\n - Intel/AMD: Often 4-6 micro-ops per cycle\n - Apple Silicon: Up to 8 instructions per cycle in some scenarios\n\n2. **Pipeline Stalls**: Not all cycles are productive\n - Cache misses\n - Branch mispredictions\n - Memory latency\n\n3. **JIT Compilation**: The JVM optimizes code at runtime\n - Inlining\n - Loop unrolling\n - Dead code elimination\n\n4. **Dynamic Frequency Scaling**: CPU frequency varies with load\n - Turbo Boost (Intel)\n - Precision Boost (AMD)\n - Dynamic frequency on Apple Silicon\n\n### Interpretation\n\nThe instruction cycle values should be interpreted as:\n- **Relative comparison tool**: Compare different operations to each other\n- **Lower bound estimate**: Real instruction count is likely lower due to parallelism\n- **Platform-specific**: Results vary by CPU architecture and speed\n\n## Usage Example\n\n```bash\n# Run all unit time tests\ntest.rununittime\n\n# Run a specific test\ntest.rununittime testname=LocalAssignment\n```\n\n### Sample Output\n\n```\nCPU Speed: 2.60 GHz (detected)\n\nms_per_unit | ns_per_unit | units | instruction_cycles | category | subcategory | description\n------------ | ----------- | ----- | ------------------ | -------- | ----------- | -----------\n0.0000004 | 0.4 | 1.0 | 1.04 | math | primitive | Local Assignment\n0.0000012 | 1.2 | 3.0 | 3.12 | math | primitive | Integer Addition\n```\n\n## Benefits\n\n1. **Hardware-Independent Metrics**: Compare performance across different CPUs\n2. **Instruction-Level Insight**: Understand approximate cost in CPU cycles\n3. **Optimization Guidance**: Identify operations that are more CPU-intensive\n4. **Automatic Detection**: No manual configuration needed for CPU speed\n\n## Platform Support\n\n- **Linux**: Full CPU detection via `/proc/cpuinfo`\n- **Mac (Intel)**: Full CPU detection via `sysctl`\n- **Mac (Apple Silicon)**: Falls back to default 4.0 GHz with warning\n- **Other Platforms**: Falls back to default 4.0 GHz with warning\n\n## Technical Notes\n\n### Precision\n- The framework already accounts for:\n - System clock precision\n - Method invocation overhead\n - Baseline unit cost (for relative \"units\" calculation)\n \n- The instruction cycle calculation adds:\n - CPU frequency-adjusted absolute cycle estimates\n - Hardware-specific timing information\n\n### Future Enhancements\n\nPotential improvements:\n1. Allow manual CPU speed override via command argument\n2. Detect performance vs. efficiency core speeds on Apple Silicon\n3. Report CPU frequency scaling ranges\n4. Add cycles-per-instruction (CPI) analysis\n5. - Integrated automatic CPU speed detection using the `CPUInfo` utility
- Added new `instruction_cycles` column to the response definition
- Detects actual CPU speed and passes it to the test runner
- Falls back to 4.0 GHz if detection fails (e.g., on Apple Silicon)

**2. `UnitTimeResult.java`**
- Added `instructionCycles` field to store the computed cycles
- Updated `toString()` and `addToRow()` methods to include the new field

**3. `UnitTimeContext.java`**
- Added `cpuGigahertz` parameter to store the CPU frequency
- Updated `runTests()` signature to accept CPU speed
- **Implemented the cycle calculation**: `instructionCycles = nsPerUnit × cpuGigahertz`

### The Formula

```
Instruction Cycles = Nanoseconds per Execution × CPU Frequency (GHz)
```

**Why it works**: At N GHz, the CPU executes N cycles per nanosecond. So multiplying the execution time (in nanoseconds) by the GHz value gives you the approximate number of clock cycles.

### Example Calculation

- **Operation**: Integer Addition
- **Time**: 1.2 nanoseconds 
- **CPU**: 2.6 GHz
- **Cycles**: 1.2 × 2.6 = **3.12 instruction cycles**

### Documentation Created

- **`INSTRUCTION_CYCLES_README.md`** - Comprehensive guide with formulas, examples, and platform notes

### Key Features

✓ **Automatic CPU detection** on Linux and Intel Macs 
✓ **Graceful fallback** to 4.0 GHz default on Apple Silicon 
✓ **New column** in test results showing instruction cycles 
✓ **Zero configuration** needed - works out of the box 
✓ **No linter errors** - all code compiles cleanly

package com.hitorro.util.startupframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.propreaders.JVSProperties;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.Fmt;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.StringUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.propaccess.PropaccessError;
import com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDefinition;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@ServiceDefinition(dependentService = {},
 shortName = "server",
 description = "Service startup service",
 debugCommands = {},
 generatedServices = true
)
public class HTServer extends RunnableService {
 public static final StringProperty NodeId = new StringProperty("node", "id of node if server is a multinodel server", null);
 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceProperty
 public final StringProperty ServerType = new StringProperty("servertype", "type of server to start", null);
 private String serverType;
 private JsonNode serverProps = null;

 public List<Class> getDependentService() {
 serverType = ServerType.apply();
 JVS jvs = JVSProperties.getProperties();
 String server = Fmt.S("services.%s", serverType);
 try {
 serverProps = jvs.get(server);
 } catch (PropaccessError propaccessError) {
 return null;
 }
 if (serverProps != null) {
 List<Class> dependencies = new ArrayList<Class>();
 for (JsonNode e : serverProps) {
 String s = e.textValue();
 Class clazz = ClassUtil.getClassForName(s, null);
 if (clazz != null) {
 dependencies.add(clazz);
 } else {
 Log.servicecontext.fatal("Dependent service %s does not have a corresponding class to initialize", s);
 }
 }
 return dependencies;
 }
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceInit
 public String init(boolean dbInit, final boolean upgrading, final long currentVersion, final long targetVersion) {
 if (serverProps == null || serverProps.size() == 0) {
 return Fmt.S("Unable to initialize HTServer, service %s is not defined in the services file.", serverType);
 }
 return null;
 }

 public String run() {
 ServiceContext.waitForDeInit();
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDeInit
 public String deInit() {
 return null;
 }

 public String getShortName() {
 String nodeId = NodeId.apply();
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(nodeId)) {
 return Fmt.S("Server-%s", ServerType.apply());
 }

 return Fmt.S("%s-%s", ServerType.apply(), nodeId);
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceStart
 public String start(boolean dbInit) {
 return null;
 }

}

import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Command;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.CommandSession;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ResponseShape;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.CommandArgument;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.CommandDef;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.RespColumn;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.ResponseDefinition;
import com.hitorro.util.core.CPUInfo;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.DoubleProperty;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;

/**
 * Copyright (c) 2003 - present HiTorro All rights reserved. User: chris Date: Nov 22, 2006 Time: 6:47:16 PM
 */
@CommandDef(command = "test.rununittime", description = "Execute unit time tests")
public class UnitTimeCommand extends Command {
 @ResponseDefinition(command = "utr",
 rowname = "utr",
 columns = {@RespColumn(name = "ms_per_unit", lName = "msperunit", type = Double.class),
					@RespColumn(name = "ns_per_unit", lName = "nsperunit", type = Double.class),
 @RespColumn(name = "units", lName = "units", type = Double.class),
 @RespColumn(name = "instruction_cycles", lName = "instructioncycles", type = Double.class),
 @RespColumn(name = "category", lName = "category"),
 @RespColumn(name = "subcategory", lName = "subcategory"),
 @RespColumn(name = "description", lName = "description"),
 @RespColumn(name = "name", lName = "name")})
 private ResponseShape responseShape = new ResponseShape();
 @CommandArgument(required = false)
 private StringProperty TestName = new StringProperty("testname", "individual test to run", "");

	private DoubleProperty GIGAHERTZ = new DoubleProperty("gh", "gigahertz", 4.0);

	public UnitTimeCommand() {
 System.out.println();
 }

 @Override
 public boolean execute(String rawValue, JVS args, Response response, CommandSession session) {
 UnitTimeContext context = new UnitTimeContext();
 String singleTest = TestName.apply(args);
 response.setResponseShape(responseShape);
 
 // Detect CPU clock speed
 double gigahertz = GIGAHERTZ.apply(args); // Default fallback
 CPUInfo.ClockSpeed cpuSpeed = CPUInfo.getCPUClockSpeed();
 if (cpuSpeed != null) {
 gigahertz = cpuSpeed.getSpeedGHz();
 Log.util.info("Detected CPU speed: %.2f GHz", gigahertz);
 } else {
 Log.util.warn("Unable to detect CPU speed, using default: %.2f GHz", gigahertz);
 }
 
 context.runTests(response, singleTest, gigahertz);
 return true;
 }

}

package com.hitorro.base.docprocessing.commands;

import com.hitorro.base.docprocessing.QueueLoaderBaseFileCrawlerCallback;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.util.basefile.fs.BaseFile;
import com.hitorro.util.basefile.fs.BaseFileSystem;
import com.hitorro.util.basefile.tools.crawler.BaseFileCrawler;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Command;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.CommandSession;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.CommandArgument;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ano.CommandDef;
import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.StringProperty;

/**
 * bags.loadtoqueue path=file://ht/docs/cheatsheets; (default queue is docs and that goes /hthome/queue/docs)
 */
@CommandDef(command = "bags.loadtoqueue", description = "Crawl a directory to find files to load into the provided queue.")
public class LoadDocsToQueue extends Command {
	@CommandArgument(required = true)
	public static final StringProperty PathKey = new StringProperty("path", "file:// or file:// path to content", null);
	@CommandArgument(required = false)
	public static final StringProperty QueueKey = new StringProperty("queue", "file:// or file:// path to content", "docs");
	@CommandArgument(required = false)
	public static final StringProperty BagtypeKey = new StringProperty("bagtype", "", "webpage");

	public boolean execute(String rawValue, JVS args, Response response, CommandSession session) throws Exception {
		String path = PathKey.apply(args);
		String queue = QueueKey.apply(args);
		String docType = BagtypeKey.apply(args);
		BaseFile bf = BaseFileSystem.getBaseFileFromPath(path);
		QueueLoaderBaseFileCrawlerCallback callback = new QueueLoaderBaseFileCrawlerCallback(queue, docType);
		BaseFileCrawler crawler = new BaseFileCrawler();
		crawler.setRoot(bf);
		crawler.setCallback(callback);
		int i = crawler.execute();
		this.writeSuccess(response, "examined %s documents, processed: %s documents", i, callback.getProcessedCount());
		return true;
	}
}

 2|
 3|## Overview
 4|
 5|Hitorro modules are managed as **independent Git repositories** using shell scripts, **NOT** as Git submodules. This approach:
 6|- ✅ Keeps each module fully independent and reusable
 7|- ✅ Allows modules to be used in other projects without Git submodule complexities
 8|- ✅ Provides simple checkout/update workflows
 9|- ✅ Maintains clean separation of concerns
 10|
 11|## Quick Start
 12|
 13|### Initial Setup (Check out all modules)
 14|
 15|```bash
 16|# Clone/update all modules on the 3.0.0 branch
 17|./checkout-modules.sh
 18|
 19|# Or specify a different branch
 20|./checkout-modules.sh main
 21|```
 22|
 23|### Daily Updates
 24|
 25|```bash
 26|# Pull latest changes for all modules
 27|./update-modules.sh
 28|
 29|# Or specify a different branch
 30|./update-modules.sh main
 31|```
 32|
 33|## Script Details
 34|
 35|### Option 1: checkout-modules.sh (Full Setup)
 36|
 37|**Purpose**: Clone missing modules or update existing ones
 38|
 39|**Usage**:
 40|```bash
 41|./checkout-modules.sh [branch-name]
 42|```
 43|
 44|**Behavior**:
 45|- If a module doesn't exist: Clones it from Git
 46|- If a module exists: Stashes local changes, switches to specified branch, pulls updates
 47|- Provides detailed color-coded output
 48|
 49|**Example**:
 50|```bash
 51|./checkout-modules.sh 3.0.0
 52|```
 53|
 54|### Option 2: update-modules.sh (Quick Update)
 55|
 56|**Purpose**: Update all existing modules (skips cloning)
 57|
 58|**Usage**:
 59|```bash
 60|./update-modules.sh [branch-name]
 61|```
 62|
 63|**Behavior**:
 64|- Only processes modules that already exist
 65|- Stashes local changes, switches to specified branch, pulls updates
 66|- Simple, quiet output
 67|
 68|**Example**:
 69|```bash
 70|./update-modules.sh
 71|```
 72|
 73|## Configuring Module URLs
 74|
 75|Edit `checkout-modules.sh` to set your actual Git repository URLs:
 76|
 77|```bash
 78|MODULES=(
 79| "hitorro-util|https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git"
 80| "hitorro-base|https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-base.git"
 81| # ... etc
 82|)
 83|```
 84|
 85|Format: `MODULE_NAME|GIT_URL`
 86|
 87|## Workflow Examples
 88|
 89|### Scenario 1: Fresh Development Environment
 90|
 91|```bash
 92|# 1. Clone the hitorro-root repository
 93|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-root.git
 94|cd hitorro-root
 95|
 96|# 2. Check out all dependent modules on version 3.0.0
 97|./checkout-modules.sh 3.0.0
 98|
 99|# 3. Build the project
100|mvn clean install
101|
102|# 4. Start developing
103|# You can now edit any module and they're all available for building
104|```
105|
106|### Scenario 2: Update to Latest Changes
107|
108|```bash
109|# Pull updates for root project
110|git pull origin 3.0.0
111|
112|# Update all modules
113|./update-modules.sh 3.0.0
114|
115|# Rebuild
116|mvn clean install
117|```
118|
119|### Scenario 3: Work on Different Branch
120|
121|```bash
122|# Checkout development branch in all repos
123|./checkout-modules.sh dev
124|
125|# Or update only (if already cloned)
126|./update-modules.sh dev
127|```
128|
129|### Scenario 4: Use Only Specific Modules
130|
131|```bash
132|# Skip update scripts - just clone what you need manually
133|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git
134|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-base.git
135|
136|# Or use the scripts and delete modules you don't need
137|./checkout-modules.sh 3.0.0
138|rm -rf hitorro-baseui hitorro-conversation # remove unwanted modules
139|```
140|
141|## Comparison with Git Submodules
142|
143|| Aspect | This Approach (Shell Scripts) | Git Submodules |
144||--------|-------------------------------|----------------|
145|| **Module Independence** | ✅ Fully independent | ⚠️ Coupled to parent repo |
146|| **Use in Other Projects** | ✅ Simple clone and use | ❌ Must be submodule or separate clone |
147|| **Learning Curve** | ✅ Simple Git operations | ❌ Complex submodule commands |
148|| **Performance** | ✅ Standard Git operations | ⚠️ Can be slower |
149|| **Merge Conflicts** | ✅ Standard Git merges | ⚠️ Submodule-specific issues |
150|| **Version Tracking** | ✅ `.gitmodules` equivalent is the script | ✅ `.gitmodules` |
151|| **Partial Checkout** | ✅ Easy (clone only what you need) | ⚠️ More complex |
152|| **Repository URL Changes** | ✅ Edit script once | ❌ Must update `.gitmodules` |
153|
154|## Why Not Git Submodules?
155|
156|Git submodules create tight coupling and complexity:
157|
158|### Problems with Git Submodules
159|
160|1. **Forced coupling**: Modules must be submodules in every project
161| ```bash
162| # Other projects must use submodules to use your modules
163| git submodule add https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git
164| ```
165|
166|2. **Complex commands**: Special submodule commands required
167| ```bash
168| git submodule update --init --recursive
169| git submodule foreach git pull origin master
170| ```
171|
172|3. **Merge/conflict issues**: Submodule pointer references can be tricky
173| ```bash
174| # Submodule commits can get out of sync
175| # Detached HEAD states common
176| ```
177|
178|4. **Independent usage**: Harder to use modules independently
179| ```bash
180| # Can't just "git clone hitorro-util" and expect it to work nicely
181| ```
182|
183|### Benefits of This Approach
184|
185|1. **Real independence**: Each module is a standalone Git repository
186| ```bash
187| # Anyone can clone and use hitorro-util
188| git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git
189| cd hitorro-util
190| mvn package # Just works!
191| ```
192|
193|2. **Simple Git operations**: No special commands needed
194| ```bash
195| # Just normal Git operations
196| cd hitorro-util
197| git pull
198| git checkout feature-branch
199| ```
200|
201|3. **Flexibility**: Use modules however/wherever you want
202| ```bash
203| # Use in any project, any way you want
204| # As normal deps in pom.xml:
205| # <dependency>
206| # <groupId>com.hitorro</groupId>
207| # <artifactId>hitorro-util</artifactId>
208| # <version>3.0.0</version>
209| # </dependency>
210| ```
211|
212|4. **Easy to start**: Clone modules where convenient
213| ```bash
214| # In this workspace:
215| ./checkout-modules.sh
216|
217| # In another project:
218| mkdir libs && cd libs
219| git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git
220| ```
221|
222|## Advanced: Custom Workspaces
223|
224|You can create different workspace configurations:
225|
226|### Option A: Minimal Workspace
227|
228|```bash
229|# Only include what you need
230|mkdir hitorro-minimal
231|cd hitorro-minimal
232|
233|# Copy checkout-modules.sh and edit MODULES array
234|# Only include: hitorro-util, hitorro-base, hitorro-app
235|
236|./checkout-modules.sh
237|```
238|
239|### Option B: Feature Workspace
240|
241|```bash
242|# Workspace for specific feature development
243|mkdir hitorro-text-workspace
244|cd hitorro-text-workspace
245|
246|# Clone only text-related modules
247|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-text-core.git
248|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-text-persistence.git
249|git clone https://github.com/geekychris/hitorro-util.git # required dependency
250|
251|# Create a minimal pom.xml referencing these
252|```
253|
254|### Option C: Development vs Production
255|
256|```bash
257|# Development: Use source code modules
258|./checkout-modules.sh dev
259|
260|# Production: Use published artifacts from Maven repo
261|# No need for script! Just add dependencies to pom.xml
262|```
263|
264|## Troubleshooting
265|
266|### Script Not Executable
267|
268|```bash
269|chmod +x checkout-modules.sh
270|chmod +x update-modules.sh
271|```
272|
273|### Wrong Branch
274|
275|```bash
276|# Update modules to correct branch
277|./update-modules.sh correct-branch-name
278|```
279|
280|### Module Already Exists But Not a Git Repo
281|
282|If you have directories that aren't Git repos:
283|```bash
284|# Remove the directory and let the script clone it
285|rm -rf hitorro-util
286|./checkout-modules.sh
287|```
288|
289|### Merge Conflicts During Update
290|
291|The script will stash changes before updating:
292|```bash
293|# To restore stashed changes
294|cd hitorro-util
295|git stash list
296|git stash pop stash@{0}
297|```
298|
299|### Network Issues
300|
301|If cloning fails due to network issues:
302|```bash
303|# The script will report failures and continue
304|# Just re-run it:
305|./checkout-modules.sh
306|```
307|
308|## Best Practices
309|
310|1. **Commit the scripts** - Keep `checkout-modules.sh` and `update-modules.sh` in your root repository
311|2. **Document branch names** - Add comments indicating which branches to use
312|3. **Version with modules** - Tag root repo alongside module versions for coordination

package com.hitorro.util.startupframework;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.JVS;
import com.hitorro.jsontypesystem.propreaders.JVSProperties;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.Fmt;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.StringUtil;

import com.hitorro.util.json.keys.propaccess.PropaccessError;
import com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDefinition;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@ServiceDefinition(dependentService = {},
 shortName = "server",
 description = "Service startup service",
 debugCommands = {},
 generatedServices = true
)
public class HTServer extends RunnableService {
 public static final StringProperty NodeId = new StringProperty("node", "id of node if server is a multinodel server", null);
 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceProperty
 public final StringProperty ServerType = new StringProperty("servertype", "type of server to start", null);
 private String serverType;
 private JsonNode serverProps = null;

 public List<Class> getDependentService() {
 serverType = ServerType.apply();
 JVS jvs = JVSProperties.getProperties();
 String server = Fmt.S("services.%s", serverType);
 try {
 serverProps = jvs.get(server);
 } catch (PropaccessError propaccessError) {
 return null;
 }
 if (serverProps != null) {
 List<Class> dependencies = new ArrayList<Class>();
 for (JsonNode e : serverProps) {
 String s = e.textValue();
 Class clazz = ClassUtil.getClassForName(s, null);
 if (clazz != null) {
 dependencies.add(clazz);
 } else {
 Log.servicecontext.fatal("Dependent service %s does not have a corresponding class to initialize", s);
 }
 }
 return dependencies;
 }
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceInit
 public String init(boolean dbInit, final boolean upgrading, final long currentVersion, final long targetVersion) {
 if (serverProps == null || serverProps.size() == 0) {
 return Fmt.S("Unable to initialize HTServer, service %s is not defined in the services file.", serverType);
 }
 return null;
 }

 public String run() {
 ServiceContext.waitForDeInit();
 return null;
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceDeInit
 public String deInit() {
 return null;
 }

 public String getShortName() {
 String nodeId = NodeId.apply();
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(nodeId)) {
 return Fmt.S("Server-%s", ServerType.apply());
 }

 return Fmt.S("%s-%s", ServerType.apply(), nodeId);
 }

 @com.hitorro.util.startupframework.phases.ServiceStart
 public String start(boolean dbInit) {
 return null;
 }

}

import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.Response;
import com.hitorro.util.commandandcontrol.ResponseShape;
import com.hitorro.util.core.Log;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassPathDeepIterator;
import com.hitorro.util.core.classes.ClassUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.core.string.StringUtil;
import com.hitorro.util.testframework.TestServerService;
import com.hitorro.unittime.primitive.BaseLineUnitTimer;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Copyright (c) 2003 - present HiTorro All rights reserved. User: chris Date: Nov 22, 2006 Time: 11:50:32 PM
 * <p/>
 * Find all timer tests that meet a criteria and then measure the amount of time taken to execute.
 * <p/>
 * We compute a number of things: 1) resolution of system clock. 2) cost of making a method call 3) cost of doing a
 * simple piece of work such as assignment that is assumed to be about 1 instruction
 * <p/>
 * From this we can compute what other things cost in both ms and machine instructions.
 */

public class UnitTimeContext {
 /* The precision, in milliseconds, of System.currentTimeMillis (). */
 public static double m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs = 0.0;

 /* The requested maximum relative error. */
 public static double error = 0.01;

 /* The minimum duration of tests needed to achieve the maximum
 relative "error". */
 public static double minExecutionTimeMsecs = 0.0;

 /* The overhead of doing one iteration of a test. */
 public static double m_invokationOverheadMSecs = 0.0;

 /* The cost of doing a local assignment, used as the machine-independent
 "unit". */
 public static double m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs = 0.0;
 private static UnitTimeContext utc = new UnitTimeContext();
 private boolean isInitialized = false;

 public static UnitTimeContext getUnitTimeContext() {
 return utc;
 }

 /**
 * During initialization we need to compute a few things:
 * <p/>
 * 1) Resolution of the system clock, this determines how much error there is in measuring runtime of a test. 2)
 * Baseline cost of making a call to a test function (so it can be subtracted out of tests). 3) Baseline unit cost.
 * Take an instruction that we know to be 1 cycle typically on a processor and use that as our "Unit". All other
 * tests are compared in terms of a baseline unit which should approximate a machine cycle.
 *
 * @param response
 * @param error
 */
 public void init(Response response, double error) {
 if (isInitialized) {
 return;
 }
 isInitialized = true;
 UnitTimeContext.error = error;

 // compute clock precision
 long totalDelta = 0;
 int loopCount = 100;
 for (int i = 0; i < loopCount; i++) {
 long t1 = System.currentTimeMillis();
 long t2 = t1;
 while (t1 >= t2) {
 t2 = System.currentTimeMillis();
 }
 totalDelta += t2 - t1;
 }
 // we took loopCount samples, so we are going to take the median
 m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs = (double) totalDelta / loopCount;

 minExecutionTimeMsecs = (1.0 / error) * m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs;
 if (response != null && response.getShape() == null) {
 ResponseShape shape = new ResponseShape("UnitTime", "row");
 shape.addHeader("execution time", "instructions", "category", "subcategory", "description", "class");
 shape.addHeaderShortNames("execution time", "instructions", "category", "subcategory", "description", "class");
 shape.addRowTypes(Double.class, Double.class, String.class, String.class, String.class, String.class);
 response.setResponseShape(shape);
 }
 // compute the cost of calling a method
 // ensure jitted
 //executeTest(null, new BaseLineUnitTimer());
 //executeTest(null, new BaseLineUnitTimer());

 m_invokationOverheadMSecs = executeTest(new BaseLineUnitTimer()).milliSecondsPerUnit;
 // compute the cost of doing a local assignment considered one unit

 m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs = executeTest(new com.hitorro.unittime.primitive.math.LocalAssignment()).milliSecondsPerUnit;
 if (m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs < 0) {
 Log.util.error("baseline unit cost is smaller than 0");
 m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs = executeTest(new com.hitorro.unittime.primitive.math.LocalAssignment()).milliSecondsPerUnit;
 }

 }


 /**
 * Run all the tests that test our criteria. We find the tests from scanning the classpath.
 *
 * @param response
 */
 public List<UnitTimeResult> runTests(Response response, String singleTest) {
 List<UnitTimeResult> results = new ArrayList();
 HashMap<String, String> map = new HashMap<String, String>();
 List<UnitTimer> timers = getTests(map);
 Collections.sort(timers, new TimersSorter());
 init(response, 0.005);
 if (StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(singleTest)) {
 for (UnitTimer timer : timers) {
 if (timer.visible()) {
 timer.setContext(this);
 UnitTimeResult utr = executeTest(timer);
 results.add(utr);
 if (response != null) {
 utr.addToRow(response);
 }
 }
 }
 } else {
 singleTest = singleTest.toLowerCase();
 for (UnitTimer timer : timers) {
 if (timer.getClass().getCanonicalName().toLowerCase().endsWith(singleTest)) {
 timer.setContext(this);
 UnitTimeResult utr = executeTest(timer);
 results.add(utr);
 if (response != null) {
 utr.addToRow(response);
 }
 }
 }
 }
 response.end();
 return results;
 }


 /**
 * Find tests in the classpath.
 *
 * @param categoryConstraint
 * @return
 */
 public List<UnitTimer> getTests(Map<String, String> categoryConstraint) {
 List<UnitTimer> testCases = new ArrayList<UnitTimer>();
 ClassPathDeepIterator iter = new ClassPathDeepIterator();
 while (iter.hasNext()) {

 String orig = iter.next();
 String c = ClassUtil.translateClassFilenameToCanonical(orig);
 if (!StringUtil.nullOrEmptyOrBlankString(c)) {
 if (!TestServerService.getInstance().isPathWithinTestPaths(c)) {
 continue;
 }
 try {
 Class cl = Class.forName(c);

 if (!ClassUtil.isAbstract(cl) && ClassUtil.isSubClass(cl, UnitTimer.class)) {
 try {
 UnitTimer test = (UnitTimer) cl.newInstance();
 if (categoryConstraint.size() == 0) {
 testCases.add(test);
 } else {
 String cat = test.getCategory().toLowerCase();
 if (categoryConstraint.get(cat) != null) {
 testCases.add(test);
 }
 }

 Log.test.debug("Added %s test to the listFiles of tests to visible", c);
 } catch (InstantiationException e) {
 Log.util.error("Unable to create instance of test %s %s", c, e, e);
 } catch (IllegalAccessException e) {
 Log.util.error("Unable to create instance of test %s %s", c, e, e);
 }
 }
 } catch (ClassNotFoundException e) {
 Log.util.error("Unable to get class for %s %e", e, e);
 }
 }
 }
 return testCases;
 }

 public final UnitTimeResult executeTest(UnitTimer unit) {
 if (isInitialized == false) {
 init(null, 0.005);
 }
 // attempt to jit.
 UnitTimeResult result = new UnitTimeResult();

 try {
 unit.init();

 unit.preTest();
 try {
 unit.test();
 } finally {
 unit.postTest();
 }

 long n = 1;
 double runTimeInMillis = 0;
 double startTimeInMillis = 0;
 double requiredExecTimeInMSecs = minExecutionTimeMsecs;


 if (unit.getTotalMsecs() > 0) {
 requiredExecTimeInMSecs = unit.getTotalMsecs();
 }

 try {
 unit.preTest();
 while (true) {
 System.gc();

 startTimeInMillis = System.currentTimeMillis();
 for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
 unit.test();
 }
 runTimeInMillis = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTimeInMillis;


 if (runTimeInMillis >= requiredExecTimeInMSecs) {
 // we have hit our target time
 break;
 } else {
 if (runTimeInMillis < 10 * m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs) {
 n = 2 * n;
 } else {
 n = (long) Math.max(1.1 * n,
 requiredExecTimeInMSecs / (runTimeInMillis - m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs) * n);
 }
 if (n < 0) {

 Log.util.error("Unit test loop overflow");
 break;
 }
 }
 }
 } finally {
 unit.postTest();
 }
 // what does it cost to make 1 call
 double individualCallTime = (runTimeInMillis / n) - m_invokationOverheadMSecs;
 if (individualCallTime < 0) {
 // we are not that precise. This call looks like it runs approx same as a invokation call
 // jit could of defeated us. I dont like negative values so lets make it a baseline unit cost
 // we should perhaps consider running the tests again
 Log.util.error("Reseting call time to baseline since it is negative (could be defeated by jit)");
 individualCallTime = m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs;
 }
 // take account that 1 call my run whatever we are testing n times, then take account of the call cost
 double milliSecondsPerUnit = (individualCallTime / unit.getIterations()) - unit.getBaseMsecsPerTest();

 // we have an approx baseline for what a unit costs to execute (proxy for instruction cycle)
 double units = milliSecondsPerUnit / m_baseLineUnitCostMSecs;

 result.milliSecondsPerUnit = milliSecondsPerUnit;
			result.nsPerUnit = milliSecondsPerUnit * 1000000;
 result.units = units;
 result.category = unit.getCategory();
 result.subCategory = unit.getSubCategory();
 result.description = unit.getDescription();
 result.unitClass = unit.getClass();

 Log.unitTime.debug("%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s",
 Double.toString(milliSecondsPerUnit),
					Double.toString(result.nsPerUnit),
 Double.toString(units),
 unit.getCategory(),
 unit.getSubCategory(),
 unit.getDescription(),
 ClassUtil.getBareName(unit.getClass()));
 if (units < 0) {
 Log.unitTime.info("Units < 0 %s, n=%s, m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs=%s", Double.toString(units), n, m_systemClockPrecisionInMsecs);
 }


 } catch (Exception e) {
 result.error = e;
 result.milliSecondsPerUnit = 0.0;
 }
 return result;
 }
}


class TimersSorter implements Comparator<UnitTimer> {

 public int compare(UnitTimer o1, UnitTimer o2) {
 int cat = o1.getCategory().compareTo(o2.getCategory());
 if (cat == 0) {
 return o1.getSubCategory().compareTo(o2.getSubCategory());
 }

 return cat;
 }
}
